THE MEASURED PROBLEM. Discovery walked up to 16 candidates (configured URL, ports 3000-3010, 4500/4555/8443, https:8443) at timeoutInterval 6s each. For a PAIRED user that walk is sequential, so a silently-dropping network cost up to ~96s of probing while swipe actions queued behind it. The comment justifying those 16 candidates claimed 'discovery is concurrent, so the extra candidates cost no wall time' — true only for the UNPAIRED sweep, not the path a real user is on. Comment corrected, since it is what invites more candidates.

WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE: the paired sweep stays sequential. Every candidate carries the Bearer token, so racing them fans the credential across sibling ports. scripts/ios-connection-stability.test.mjs already pinned this ('Bearer tokens are not sent to speculative sibling ports') and my first draft tripped it — the existing guard worked. Only its call signature was updated.

DELIVERED:
1. Last-good base URL persisted per host and tried first, so the ordinary reconnect (same desktop, same port) is ONE probe. Keyed by host so a remembered port never leaks to another desktop; honoured only while still a candidate; dropped by clear() on disconnect.
2. The preferred endpoint is probed ALONE before any fan-out — which also keeps it authoritative, so timing cannot relocate the user to a port they never chose.
3. The unpaired sweep cancels remaining probes once the answer is settled.
Preferred-probe failures are seeded into the fallback's adjudication so the diagnosis still reflects the configured endpoint.

REVIEW CATCH, a real semantic regression: my first short-circuit cancelled on the first .ok to ARRIVE, letting a later candidate win purely on timing. Candidate order is a PREFERENCE ranking (3000 before 3001, :8443 before bare 443), so discovery could relocate to and persist a lower-ranked port. Probing candidates[0] alone masked it for the head of the list but said nothing about ordering among the rest — I had anticipated the race and under-mitigated it. The sweep now stops only once a candidate has succeeded AND every candidate ranked above it has reported.
